text: MMA (Mastitis Metritis Agalactia) is a common sow problem, generally from bacterial invasion of the udder and resulting toxin production; vulval discharge and constipation are often seen alongside it. Signs usually appear within 12 hours of farrowing: pressing the teats produces no milk flow and piglets go hungry; the sow doesn't eat after delivery and shows depression and restlessness when piglets try to suckle; a slight fever (40–41°C) may be present. This is an emergency — if piglets can't nurse quickly, they miss colostrum antibodies and become weak, cold, and inactive, setting up ideal conditions for diarrhea. Treatment: inject 0.5 ml oxytocin into the blood, which triggers milk ejection within seconds (have piglets ready to nurse right before injecting); inject TMP+Sulfa to control E. coli in the udder; inject Dexamethasone if the udder is hard and hot; and give piglets special care — help weaker ones reach the teats and prepare a warm, comfortable nest to prevent chilling.
